doc.title: Anat Cohen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 9, 2021

title: Oded Lev-Ari, Anzic Records and the tentet
summary: Her high school friend Oded runs Anzic Records, directs the tentet and wrote the Triple Helix concerto; Putty Boy Strut is Flying Lotus's.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Okay. Do you have someone who has given you career advice over the years?

Wow. There’s little mentors, there’s little phrases here and there, but you know there’s career and then there’s music and there’s a lot of elements to my journey. But a person that has been extremely helpful and by my side as far as suggestions and support and running our record label is Oded Lev-Ari. Oded is my high school friend and he is the musical director of the tentet, the project that we have together, and he’s also the person that really runs Anzic Records because all the albums that I recorded came out on our own label, a label we established together in 2007, 5, 7. And so, and he is a brilliant musician, a brilliant man, brilliant at so many things, and has a vision for, you know, supports me, knows me, and tells me the truth and by my side in my releases and business advice but also ideas. It’s good to have somebody like that in my life. I think I would really be lost without him. And of course, okay sure, let’s talk about Oded and then we’ll talk about my brothers.
Okay. I just was curious if he composed this song “Putty Boy Strut”?

No the song “Putty Boy Strut” was composed by Flying Lotus, also known as Steve Allison. But Oded composed a concerto for the tentet and myself that we premiered in Carnegie Hall a couple of years ago and it’s the title album “Triple Helix” is the name of the concerto, it’s also the title album of the last tentet album that was nominated for a Grammy for best large ensemble. Exciting.
